In this in vitro cadaver study, researchers investigated the impact of tricompartmental vs. unicompartmental knee replacement on knee kinematics. The results showed that unicompartmental knee replacement (UKR) preserved normal knee kinematics, while the tricompartmental replacement significantly altered knee kinematics.

The study suggests that UKR is a viable option for patients with unicompartmental knee osteoarthritis who are seeking to restore their natural knee function and alleviate symptoms. The findings of this in vitro cadaver study provide valuable insights into the effects of different knee replacement options on knee kinematics, which can inform clinical decision-making.

It's essential to note that each patient is unique, and individual results may vary. Your healthcare provider will be able to assess your specific needs and make an informed decision about the best course of treatment for you.
